grammar_focus: enough 的位置(well enough / enough time / hot enough to do)、现在分词表伴随(smashing / sending)、discover 与 invent 的区别、beside 与 besides 的区别、had to do(不得不·实际做了)与 should have done(本应做却没做)(原创承载 NCE3 L33 考点·轻净化+美式化:啤酒瓶→汽水瓶、去掉宝宝划伤细节;挡风玻璃 windshield、卡车 truck、初学司机 student driver、故事移到芝加哥郊区·连环倒霉喜剧内核原样保留)
scene: 我们都经历过诸事不顺的日子。一天也许开头还算顺利,可突然之间,一切好像都失了控。总是这样:一大堆事情偏偏挑在同一刻出岔子,仿佛一件不起眼的小事引发了一连串连锁反应。假设你正一边做饭,一边照看宝宝。这时电话响了——这成了一连串意外灾祸的序幕。你在讲电话,宝宝一把扯下桌布,打碎了你一半的好瓷器。你匆匆挂断电话,去收拾宝宝和碎瓷片。与此同时,饭菜煮糊了。仿佛这还不够让你崩溃,你丈夫回来了,还意外地带回三位客人来吃晚饭。事情也能大规模地出岔子,枫叶镇——芝加哥的一个郊区——最近就有不少人领教了这一点。一天傍晚的高峰时段,两辆车相撞,两位司机都吵了起来。紧跟在这两辆车后面的,恰好是一位初学开车的女司机。她一下子慌了神,把车停住了。这一停,让跟在她后面的司机猛踩刹车。那司机的妻子正坐在他旁边,手里捧着一个大蛋糕。她被向前一甩,蛋糕直接穿过挡风玻璃,落在了马路上。一个正驶近、与那辆车并排的卡车司机,看见一个蛋糕在空中飞,猛地停了车。卡车上装满了空汽水瓶,几百个瓶子从车尾滑落,滚到了马路上。这又引发了一场怒气冲冲的争吵。与此同时,后面的车堵成了一片。警察花了将近一个小时才让交通重新动起来。这期间,卡车司机不得不扫起几百个碎瓶子。这场混乱里只有两条流浪狗得了好处,它们贪婪地把剩下的蛋糕一扫而光。这真是倒霉透顶的一天!

grammar_card.title: enough 的位置 / 现在分词表伴随 / discover vs invent / beside vs besides / had to vs should have
grammar_card.intro: ①enough 放在形容词/副词之后(good enough / well enough),但放在名词之前(enough time);“…到足以…”用 形容词 + enough + to do(hot enough to burn)。②现在分词表示同时发生的伴随动作:pulled the cloth off, smashing the dishes。③discover 是“发现(本已存在的)”,invent 是“发明(原来没有的)”。④beside 是“在…旁边”,besides 是“除…之外(还)”。⑤had to do=不得不(实际做了);should have done=本应做却没做。

rows: had to do / should have done

specialRules.rule: enough 修饰形容词/副词时放其后(warm enough),修饰名词时放其前(enough money);“形容词 + enough + to do”表示“…到足以…”。
beside=在…旁边(sit beside me);besides=除…之外还有(besides the cake, …)。一字之差意思不同。
美式:windshield(英式 windscreen)、truck(英式 lorry)、student driver(英式 learner driver)、soda(英式 fizzy drink)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What began the series of traffic accidents?
options: A student driver panicked and stopped her car
A dog ran into the street

passage: We have all experienced days when everything goes wrong. A day may begin well enough, but suddenly everything seems to get out of control. What invariably happens is that a great number of things choose to go wrong at precisely the same moment. It is as if a single unimportant event set up a chain of reactions. Suppose that you are preparing a meal and keeping an eye on the baby at the same time. The telephone rings, and this marks the prelude to an unforeseen series of catastrophes. While you are on the phone, the baby pulls the tablecloth off the table, smashing half your best crockery. You hang up hurriedly and attend to the baby and the broken dishes. Meanwhile, the meal gets burnt. As if this were not enough to reduce you to tears, your husband arrives, unexpectedly bringing three guests to dinner. Things can go wrong on a big scale, as a number of people recently discovered in Maplewood, a suburb of Chicago. During the rush hour one evening, two cars collided and both drivers began to argue. The woman immediately behind the two cars happened to be a student driver. She suddenly got into a panic and stopped her car. This made the driver following her brake hard. His wife was sitting beside him holding a large cake. As she was thrown forward, the cake went right through the windshield and landed on the road. Seeing a cake flying through the air, a truck driver who was drawing up alongside the car pulled up all of a sudden. The truck was loaded with empty soda bottles, and hundreds of them slid off the back of the vehicle and onto the road. This led to yet another angry argument. Meanwhile, the traffic piled up behind. It took the police nearly an hour to get the traffic on the move again. In the meantime, the truck driver had to sweep up hundreds of broken bottles. Only two stray dogs benefited from all this confusion, for they greedily devoured what was left of the cake. It was just one of those days!

stage5.stem: "A day may begin well ___."(表"足够",放在形容词/副词后面的那个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 一天可能开头还算顺利。

stage5.stem: "There wasn't ___ time to cook the meal."(表"足够的",放在名词前面的那个词)
"The soup was ___ to burn my tongue."("热到足以烫舌":形容词在前、表"足够"的词在后,再 + to do)
"The baby pulled the cloth off, ___ half the dishes."(现在分词表同时发生"打碎了…")
stage5.stem_cn: 宝宝把桌布扯下,打碎了一半盘子。

stage5.stem: "She was thrown forward, ___ the cake through the window."(现在分词表伴随)
stage5.stem_cn: 她被向前甩去,把蛋糕从窗户甩了出去。

stage5.stem: "The bottles slid off the truck, ___ all over the road."(现在分词表伴随)
stage5.stem_cn: 瓶子从卡车上滑落,滚了一地。

stage5.stem: "Columbus is said to have ___ America."("发现"原本就存在的东西用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 据说哥伦布发现了美洲。

stage5.stem: "Edison ___ the light bulb."("发明"原来没有的东西用哪个)
"A number of people recently ___ how badly a day can go."("发现、意识到(事实)"用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 最近有些人发现,一天能糟到什么地步。

stage5.stem: "His wife was sitting ___ him in the car."("在…旁边"用哪个)
"___ the cake, there was nothing else to eat."("除…之外(还)"用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 除了蛋糕,没别的可吃了。

stage5.stem: "Come and sit ___ me."("坐在我身边"用哪个)
"The truck driver ___ sweep up hundreds of bottles."("不得不(实际做了)"用 ___ do)
stage5.stem_cn: 卡车司机不得不扫起几百个瓶子。

stage5.stem: "You ___ told me earlier; now it's too late."("本应做却没做"的语气)
stage5.stem_cn: 你本该早点告诉我,现在太晚了。

stage5.stem: "Because the road was blocked, we ___ wait an hour."("不得不(结果做了)"用 ___ wait)
stage5.stem_cn: 因为路被堵,我们只好等了一小时。

stage5.stem: "A sudden terrible disaster is a ___."("大祸、灾难"用哪个词)
"When two cars crash into each other, they ___."("猛撞、相撞"用哪个词)
"To eat something quickly and hungrily is to ___ it."("狼吞虎咽地吃"用哪个词)
